summary: Checks whether a value is an email address.
description: The address is split at a single `@`: the domain is checked the way `isValidDomain` checks one, and the local part must be non-empty and free of spaces. It is a format check, not proof that the mailbox exists.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is an email address; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
isEmail("user@example.com"); // => true
isEmail("first.last@sub.example.co.uk"); // => true
isEmail("user@@example.com"); // => false
isEmail("user@"); // => false
isEmail("example.com"); // => false
isEmail(""); // => false
```
